title: Binding product distributions coordinatewise
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $A$, and for each $a\in A$ let $q(a)$ be a probability mass function on $B$. For every natural number $n$, first sample an independent $n$-tuple from $p$ and then, independently at each coordinate conditional on that tuple, sample from the corresponding law $q(a)$. The resulting distribution on $B^n$ is the independent product distribution whose coordinate law is the mixture of $q(a)$ over $a$ drawn from $p$.
hypotheses_covered: A probability mass function $q(a)$ on $B$ for every $a\in A$
